topic: The ionosphere: MUF, LUF, regions, scatter and NVIS (G3B, G3C; 23 pool questions)

questions.question: What is a characteristic of skywave signals arriving at your location by both short-path and long-path propagation?

choices.A: Periodic fading approximately every 10 seconds
choices.C: The signal might be cancelled causing severe attenuation
choices.D: A slightly delayed echo might be heard

questions.answer: A slightly delayed echo might be heard

questions.question: What factors affect the MUF?

choices.A: Path distance and location
choices.C: Solar radiation and ionospheric disturbances
choices.D: All these choices are correct

questions.answer: All these choices are correct

questions.question: Which frequency will have the least attenuation for long-distance skip propagation?

choices.A: Just below the MUF
choices.C: Just below the critical frequency
choices.D: Just above the critical frequency

questions.answer: Just below the MUF

questions.question: Which of the following is a way to determine current propagation on a desired band from your station?

choices.A: Use a network of automated receiving stations on the internet to see where your transmissions are being received
choices.C: Send a series of dots and listen for echoes
choices.D: All these choices are correct

questions.answer: Use a network of automated receiving stations on the internet to see where your transmissions are being received

questions.question: How does the ionosphere affect radio waves with frequencies below the MUF and above the LUF?

choices.A: They are refracted back to Earth
choices.C: They are amplified by interaction with the ionosphere
choices.D: They are refracted and trapped in the ionosphere to circle Earth

questions.answer: They are refracted back to Earth

questions.question: What usually happens to radio waves with frequencies below the LUF?

choices.A: They are refracted back to Earth
choices.C: They are attenuated before reaching the destination
choices.D: They are refracted and trapped in the ionosphere to circle Earth

questions.answer: They are attenuated before reaching the destination

questions.question: What does LUF stand for?

choices.A: The Lowest Usable Frequency for communications between two specific points
choices.B: The Lowest Usable Frequency for communications to any point outside a 100-mile radius
choices.C: The Lowest Usable Frequency during a 24-hour period
choices.D: The Lowest Usable Frequency during the past 60 minutes

questions.answer: The Lowest Usable Frequency for communications between two specific points

questions.question: What does MUF stand for?

choices.A: The Minimum Usable Frequency for communications between two points
choices.B: The Maximum Usable Frequency for communications between two points
choices.C: The Minimum Usable Frequency during a 24-hour period
choices.D: The Maximum Usable Frequency during a 24-hour period

questions.answer: The Maximum Usable Frequency for communications between two points

questions.question: What is the approximate maximum distance along the Earth’s surface normally covered in one hop using the F2 region?

choices.A: 180 miles
choices.C: 2,500 miles
choices.D: 12,000 miles

questions.answer: 2,500 miles

questions.question: What is the approximate maximum distance along the Earth’s surface normally covered in one hop using the E region?

choices.A: 180 miles
choices.C: 2,500 miles
choices.D: 12,000 miles

questions.answer: 1,200 miles

questions.question: What happens to HF propagation when the LUF exceeds the MUF?

choices.A: Propagation via ordinary skywave communications is not possible over that path
choices.B: HF communications over the path are enhanced
choices.C: Double-hop propagation along the path is more common
choices.D: Propagation over the path on all HF frequencies is enhanced

questions.answer: Propagation via ordinary skywave communications is not possible over that path

questions.question: Which of the following is typical of the lower HF frequencies during the summer?

choices.A: Poor propagation at any time of day
choices.C: Heavy distortion on signals due to photon absorption
choices.D: High levels of atmospheric noise or static

questions.answer: High levels of atmospheric noise or static

questions.question: Which ionospheric region is closest to the surface of Earth?

choices.A: The D region
choices.C: The F1 region
choices.D: The F2 region

questions.answer: The D region

questions.question: What is meant by the term “critical frequency” at a given incidence angle?

choices.A: The highest frequency which is refracted back to Earth
choices.B: The lowest frequency which is refracted back to Earth
choices.C: The frequency at which the signal-to-noise ratio approaches unity
choices.D: The frequency at which the signal-to-noise ratio is 6 dB

questions.answer: The highest frequency which is refracted back to Earth

questions.question: Why is skip propagation via the F2 region longer than that via the other ionospheric regions?

choices.A: Because it is the densest
choices.C: Because it is the highest
choices.D: Because of temperature inversions

questions.answer: Because it is the highest

questions.question: What does the term “critical angle” mean, as applied to radio wave propagation?

choices.A: The long path azimuth of a distant station
choices.B: The short path azimuth of a distant station
choices.C: The lowest takeoff angle that will return a radio wave to Earth under specific ionospheric conditions
choices.D: The highest takeoff angle that will return a radio wave to Earth under specific ionospheric conditions

questions.answer: The highest takeoff angle that will return a radio wave to Earth under specific ionospheric conditions

questions.question: Why is long-distance communication on the 40-, 60-, 80-, and 160-meter bands more difficult during the day?

choices.A: The F region absorbs signals at these frequencies during daylight hours
choices.B: The F region is unstable during daylight hours
choices.C: The D region absorbs signals at these frequencies during daylight hours
choices.D: The E region is unstable during daylight hours

questions.answer: The D region absorbs signals at these frequencies during daylight hours

questions.question: What is a characteristic of HF scatter?

choices.A: Phone signals have high intelligibility
choices.C: There are very large, sudden swings in signal strength
choices.D: Scatter propagation occurs only at night

questions.answer: Signals have a fluttering sound

questions.question: What makes HF scatter signals often sound distorted?

choices.A: The ionospheric region involved is unstable
choices.B: Ground waves are absorbing much of the signal
choices.C: The E region is not present
choices.D: Energy is scattered into the skip zone through several different paths

questions.answer: Energy is scattered into the skip zone through several different paths

questions.question: Why are HF scatter signals in the skip zone usually weak?

choices.A: Only a small part of the signal energy is scattered into the skip zone
choices.B: Signals are scattered from the magnetosphere, which is not a good reflector
choices.C: Propagation is via ground waves, which absorb most of the signal energy
choices.D: Propagation is via ducts in the F region, which absorb most of the energy

questions.answer: Only a small part of the signal energy is scattered into the skip zone

questions.question: What type of propagation allows signals to be heard in the transmitting station’s skip zone?

choices.A: Faraday rotation
choices.C: Chordal hop
choices.D: Short-path

questions.answer: Scatter

questions.question: What is near vertical incidence skywave (NVIS) propagation?

choices.A: Propagation near the MUF
choices.B: Short distance MF or HF propagation at high elevation angles
choices.C: Long path HF propagation at sunrise and sunset
choices.D: Double hop propagation near the LUF

questions.answer: Short distance MF or HF propagation at high elevation angles

questions.question: Which ionospheric region is the most absorbent of signals below 10 MHz during daylight hours?

choices.A: The F2 region
choices.C: The E region
choices.D: The D region

questions.answer: The D region
